bill.title: Grants from Bureau of Criminal Apprehension to local law enforcement clarified as reimbursements, law related to recording of crimes updated, process for determining how certain criminal records are ineligible for sealing established, and court required to provide order for protection for access by law enforcement.

posted_text:
👮 MN HF 3827 — Minnesota Bill Could Boost Local Crime Fight with State Funding

Minnesota could significantly bolster its local law enforcement efforts with this bill.

It clarifies how the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension can reimburse local agencies for investigations – specifically targeting cross-jurisdictional drug cases and providing support for victims of domestic abuse, including housing, transportation, and financial assistance.

The bill also establishes a detailed process for tracking and reporting on these reimbursements, ensuring accountability and transparency.

Importantly, it updates procedures for issuing and sharing ‘no contact’ orders, requiring law enforcement to include offender photos and immediately forwarding order information to relevant agencies within 24 hours.

Finally, the bill streamlines the process for eligible individuals to have their criminal records expunged, with the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension responsible for identifying qualifying records and making initial eligibility determinations.

Jan. 1, 2027: Effective date.
